intended_object: This is a function on binary words that encodes the outer wrapper of the completed permanent-approximation algorithm. It checks the nonnegativity bit, then either runs the nonnegative branch or outputs the encoding of 0. The docstring and the module documentation describe it this way.
explanation: This definition is an implementation detail. It is the finite-word (machine-level) version of the library's `completedAlgorithm`, built so the library can prove that the algorithm is polynomial-time computable (membership in `Complexity.FP`). It just composes the library's own encoding primitives: `machineIfHead` branches on `machineMatrixNonnegativeBit`, and the false case returns `rationalBinaryCode 0`. It does not stand for any object in the mathematical literature, so there is no standard definition to compare it with. Its body matches its docstring: nonnegative inputs go to the completed branch, and inputs that fail the sign test get the encoding of 0.
